name: Irving R. Abel et al., USP 4411499, 11.9x compact infrared telescope (Smith, Modern Lens Design, Fig. 21.12)
notes: Warren J. Smith, Modern Lens Design, 2nd ed., Figure 21.12, p. 407. Book: EFL -11750.0, BFL 1026, NA 0.0058 (F/105.3), GIH 330.78 (HFOV=1.61), PTZ/F -0.5364, VL 212.24, infinite conjugate. Wavelengths 10, 8, 12 um as in the book (primary first). Glass: GERMA entered as 4.003476 (constant index inside the book's rounded 4.003, chosen to match the book's EFL; the telescope is so nearly afocal that its EFL follows the fourth decimal of the germanium index); ZNSIR entered as ZNS_BROAD (zinc sulfide, Zemax INFRARED catalog). The book does not mark the stop; it is placed at surface 1, the front window. Infrared materials come from the Zemax INFRARED catalog; the book lists their indices at the primary wavelength from older data, so small differences in EFL are expected. Afocal 11.9x catadioptric telescope: a zinc sulfide window, a concave conic primary mirror, a germanium Mangin secondary whose aspheric rear surface reflects (surfaces 5 to 7, the same front surface twice), and a germanium eyepiece behind the primary. The table gives thicknesses without sign; spaces after an odd number of reflections are entered negative, which reproduces the book's VL. The book labels the Mangin exit surface "mirror" and the reflecting rear surface GERMA; the reflecting surface is entered as the mirror. Conic constants (kappa) and aspheric terms (ad, ae, af on r^4, r^6, r^8) as in the book. As in the book (Afo), an ideal lens of focal length 1000 follows the telescope so it can be evaluated at a finite focus; the book prints the space after it as 0.000 ("Afo Unsupported"), so the image is placed 1000 behind it. EPD = |EFL|/F# (111.59). The book's VL 212.24 leaves out the 26.416 air space before the ideal lens. Central obscuration is not modelled. Discrepancy with the book: with germanium at 4.00348 the EFL matches, but the paraxial image lies about 998 behind the ideal lens instead of the book's 1026. Book lists sa 0.0 on some surfaces; left as automatic semi-diameter.
